investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract evidence gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never reached a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the cluster's physical capacity.

Tertiary — resource quota or limit range on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource: a namespace or cluster-level quota may cap the number of peer-pod VMs that can be requested concurrently, causing exhaustion even if physical node capacity exists.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883): if cleanup failed in a previous run, those VMs would continue to hold the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract evidence gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never reached a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the cluster's physical capacity.

Tertiary — resource quota or limit range on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource: a namespace or cluster-level quota may cap the number of peer-pod VMs that can be requested concurrently, causing exhaustion even if physical node capacity exists.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883): if cleanup failed in a previous run, those VMs would continue to hold the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.
